subject.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine

question: Should OpenClaw core continue with this rescue watchdog runtime after the current-main cron/protocol/store gaps and real proof are fixed, or should the work pause for a narrower product/security design?
rationale: The PR adds a core self-repair surface that can probe, restart, and run repair commands, so maintainers must choose the product and security boundary before accepting the feature even after mechanical integration fixes.

options.title: Fix and continue the core watchdog path
options.body: Require a rebase that preserves command cron jobs, updates current protocol and SQLite storage, and provides real recovery proof before another merge review.

options.title: Pause for a smaller approved design
options.body: Hold the branch until maintainers split the recovery surface into narrower reviewed pieces with explicit operator policy.

options.title: Close in favor of the canonical design issue
options.body: Close the PR if maintainers decide the current branch is too stale or too broad to salvage safely.

recommendation.title: Fix and continue the core watchdog path
recommendation.body: Require a rebase that preserves command cron jobs, updates current protocol and SQLite storage, and provides real recovery proof before another merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest local source-history routing signal is the recent cron/protocol/store refactor that now owns the conflicting current-main surfaces.
